tldr_label: TL;DR: October PCE inflation hits 3.8%, the US proposes tariffs of 15% to 35% on 14 economies, and Wall Street claws back from an intraday Nasdaq bear market be

tldr_bullets.label: Fed
tldr_bullets.body: PCE inflation rose to 3.8% in October and core to 3.3%, above forecasts. The data cements expectations of a December 9 Fed rate hike. [[TAG:danger:hot print]]

tldr_bullets.label: Tariffs
tldr_bullets.body: USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including China, the EU and Japan. Comments are open until January 5, and China and the EU pushed back. [[TAG:warning:trade war]]

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The Nasdaq 100 briefly fell into a bear market before a late rebound, and the Dow erased an 1,100-point loss. US markets are closed for Thanksgiving. [[TAG:warning:volatile]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Ukraine said it hit five jets at Russia's Savasleyka airbase. The FT reported the US has shelved business incentives for Moscow in favor of land-for-peace talks. [[TAG:info:strategy shift]]

tldr_bullets.label: Gulf
tldr_bullets.body: Trump said the Iran war is funded through January. The Houthis stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, and the IRGC claimed more tanker mine strikes. [[TAG:danger:escalation]]

sections.title: The Fed: Hot Print
sections.summary: October PCE rises to 3.8% and core to 3.3%, cementing a December hike

paragraphs.heading: The Numbers
paragraphs.body: Morningstar reported October PCE inflation of 3.8%, in line with expectations and up from 3.6%. StockAnalysis reported core prices beat forecasts, at 3.3% against an expected 3.2%. Quartz said real consumer spending was essentially flat while personal income rose. [[TAG:danger:core beat]]

paragraphs.heading: Policy
paragraphs.body: Tl;dr Daily News said the print solidifies a December rate hike, and Traders4Traders called it the Fed's last clean read before the December 9 decision. The next PCE report is due December 23. [[TAG:warning:Dec 9]]

sections.sources: Morningstar, StockAnalysis, Quartz, tl;dr Daily News, Traders4Traders

sections.title: Trade: Tariffs on 14 Economies
sections.summary: USTR proposes 15% to 35% Section 301 duties; China calls it unilateral, EU rejects premise

paragraphs.heading: The Proposal
paragraphs.body: Holland and Knight, Kelley Drye and Legal500 reported that USTR made affirmative findings in 14 of 16 excess-capacity investigations and proposed tariffs. The economies include China, the EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, India and Vietnam, and decisions on Mexico and Norway were deferred. Traders Agency reported rates of 15% to 35%, with allies capped at 15%. Comments run until January 5, with hearings in January, so nothing is final. [[TAG:warning:proposed]]

paragraphs.heading: Pushback
paragraphs.body: France 24 reported that China, the EU and other major economies called the plan unacceptable. China's commerce ministry called the investigation unilateral and reserved the right to respond. The EU said it expects the US to honor last year's 15% deal. Particle reported higher conditional penalties for China. Reported China rates conflict across sources. [[TAG:danger:retaliation risk]]

sections.title: Markets: A Deep V
sections.summary: Nasdaq 100 briefly hits bear territory before rebound; Asia rises as US takes holiday

paragraphs.heading: Wednesday
paragraphs.body: Motley Fool and Yahoo Finance reported the Dow erased an 1,100-point loss to close higher after a late comeback. Cappnotes put the Dow up 0.33% at 50,182.95 and the Nasdaq down 0.62% at 23,585.80. Yahoo Finance reported the Nasdaq 100 flirted with bear-market territory, down 20% from its October high, and Longbridge described a deep V reversal. Bloomberg argued the selloff is unraveling the AI trade's circular deals. [[TAG:warning:bear touch]]

paragraphs.heading: Thursday
paragraphs.body: WSLS, carrying AP, reported world shares pushed higher Thursday, led by AI stocks, while US markets were closed for Thanksgiving. Oninvest reported Asian markets rose despite Trump's tariff plans. Index figures varied by source. [[TAG:info:holiday]]

sections.title: Ukraine: Airbase Hit, Pitch Changed
sections.summary: Ukraine says five jets hit at Savasleyka; US reportedly drops business lures for Moscow

paragraphs.heading: Savasleyka
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera, Ukrainska Pravda and AeroTime reported that Ukraine's General Staff said its forces hit three MiG-31s and two Su-34s at Russia's Savasleyka airbase east of Moscow. New Voice of Ukraine said the base is home to MiG-31K jets that carry Kinzhal missiles. Russia did not immediately comment, and the damage claims are Ukraine's alone. [[TAG:info:Ukrainian claim]]

paragraphs.heading: Peace Track
paragraphs.body: US News, Meduza and European Pravda, citing the Financial Times, reported the Trump administration has shelved plans to entice Russia with business ventures and shifted back to a land-for-peace approach. US News, carrying Reuters, said a US official called the report inaccurate. [[TAG:warning:disputed]]

sections.title: Gulf: Funded Through January
sections.summary: Trump says Iran war funded into January; Houthis hit Saudi targets; IRGC claims mine strikes

paragraphs.heading: Washington
paragraphs.body: WSBT and Gulf News reported Trump said the Iran war is funded through January, when an incoming Democratic Congress could curb it. The New Arab reported Trump said there is no rush on Iran. [[TAG:info:January]]

paragraphs.heading: Houthis and Hormuz
paragraphs.body: The New Arab and CNBC reported the Houthis stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including a claimed strike on a Saudi refinery. These claims are the Houthis' own. ABC News and Oilprice.com reported IRGC claims that two more tankers hit mines, which Reuters could not verify. Arab News reported an IRGC claim that an LNG tanker caught fire. sections.title: Israel: Closing In
sections.summary: Liberman says coalition possible by next week; Likud expects to be left out; Gaza strikes go on

paragraphs.heading: Coalition
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel reported Liberman said Eisenkot can form a coalition with a clear Jewish majority by the end of next week, and that the bloc is fighting over ministries. The Jerusalem Post reported Likud officials expect Eisenkot to form a government without them, and that Netanyahu urged UTJ not to rush into a deal. Yahoo said Eisenkot is closer to ousting Netanyahu. [[TAG:info:UTJ key]]

paragraphs.heading: Gaza
paragraphs.body: ClickOrlando, carrying AP, reported Israeli strikes killed eight in Gaza overnight, while Arab News reported nine killed, including a deputy education minister. The Times of Israel reported Netanyahu signaled to Kushner he is willing to move forward on the Gaza plan. [[TAG:danger:tolls differ]]

sections.title: Also Watching
sections.summary: Bank of Korea hikes to 3.25%; Ramaphosa wins Phala Phala court ruling

paragraphs.heading: Seoul Hikes
paragraphs.body: The Korea Herald, Korea Times and Al Jazeera reported the Bank of Korea raised its benchmark rate by a quarter point to 3.25% and sharply upgraded its growth forecasts. Korea JoongAng Daily reported growth forecasts of 3.9% for 2026 and 4.1% for 2027. Two board members dissented in favor of holding. [[TAG:warning:tightening]]

paragraphs.heading: South Africa
paragraphs.body: The Citizen reported President Ramaphosa won a court ruling in the Phala Phala case, which set aside a panel report that had opened the way to impeachment proceedings. An appeal is possible. [[TAG:info:court win]]
